About the role...

Join us to build Duolingo Ads, Duolingo’s premium programmatic business. Most learners use our free, ad‑supported app—so great ads are core to our mission. Reporting into the Head of Ad Sales, the Ad Sales Lead, Programmatic will build a deal‑led book of business with agency holding companies, independent agencies, and advertisers who want access to Duolingo’s native formats, first‑party learner signals, and one of the most engaged mobile audiences in the world. You will own buy‑side relationships across holdco investment and programmatic teams, trading desks, curation and principal media groups, and premium programmatic buyers. This is a high‑ownership, high‑visibility, early‑stage opportunity to help define how programmatic can fuel high‑quality ads for millions of learners while driving outcomes for partners.

🧠 You will...

• Own a programmatic revenue target and forecast, and build a predictable pipeline across agency holding‑company programmatic and investment teams, trading desks, independent agencies, and premium programmatic buyers.

• Lead our shift from open auction to premium, deal‑led PMP/PG by packaging Duolingo’s native formats and first‑party learner signals into always‑on and custom deals that buyers will pay a premium for, and negotiate annual and upfront commitments that make that revenue durable.

• Become the person holdco programmatic teams call about mobile app inventory: run joint business planning; get Duolingo onto preferred supply paths, curated marketplaces, and principal/outcome‑based buys; and defend our position when buyers consolidate

• Build the programmatic value proposition and measurement story through proposals, pricing narratives, and post‑campaign proof that connect our native formats and audience data to brand and performance outcomes (e.g., verification, attention, brand lift, incrementality, MMM).

• Partner with Ad Platform Operations and Ad Ops on deal setup, targeting, floors, pacing, and troubleshooting—ensuring what you sell is deliverable and delivers against expectations.

• Work alongside our direct sellers under clear rules of engagement so programmatic expands the account through incremental value; coordinate with Account Management pre‑ and post‑sale to drive renewal and expansion.

• Feed structured market intelligence back to sales, product, and engineering leadership about what buyers need in pricing, packaging, audience segments, formats, and integrations, balancing this input with our learner‑first standards and operational quality.

• Establish the operating rhythm for a scaling programmatic business via account planning, outreach cadences, deal hygiene in CRM, pipeline rigor, and repeatable playbooks the next sellers can run.

✅ You have...

• 8+ years in digital advertising, including at least 4 years selling programmatic on the sell side (publisher/platform/app) or in a holding‑company programmatic/investment role, carrying and hitting a quota; demonstrated PMP/PG selling and trading‑desk engagement.

• A demonstrated book of PMP and PG business you personally sourced, negotiated, and grew.

• Experience selling premium mobile or consumer app inventory—especially video and native/custom formats—through programmatic channels to top‑tier advertisers and agencies.

• Strong understanding of ad tech and mobile app ecosystems, including DSP/SSP workflows, deal IDs, verification/measurement, and using data to inform pricing and packaging.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills; clear, concise storytelling for both technical and non‑technical audiences.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Deep, current relationships with programmatic leads at major agency holding companies and larger independents.

• Experience moving partners from a heavy open‑auction mix to meaningful always‑on/custom PMP/PG alongside direct sales—and knowing what actually moved the deal (packaging, pricing, supply path, or sales motion).

• Sold against first‑party audience segments or custom data products, not just inventory.

• Hands‑on partnership with Ad Ops on deal setup, SSP onboarding, and campaign QA to improve fill, CPMs, and delivery quality.

We’re hiring a People Relations Business Partner to lead Duolingo’s approach to employee relations, leaves of absence, and workplace accommodations. You will serve as a trusted advisor to Duos, managers, and People Business Partners, bringing sound judgment and consistency to complex employee matters. You’ll manage employee relations cases, own our leave and accommodations programs, and use insights across this work to strengthen our practices and employee experience as Duolingo grows globally.

🧠 You will...

•
Employee Relations

• Manage Employee Relations Cases: Lead employee relations matters from intake through resolution, including employee concerns, workplace conflicts, conduct issues, and other sensitive situations.

• Conduct Investigations: Lead fair, thorough, and timely workplace investigations, documenting findings and partnering with Legal and People Business Partners on appropriate next steps.

• Advise Managers & PBPs: Provide practical guidance on employee concerns, performance and conduct matters, policy interpretation, and complex workplace situations.

• Build ER Practices: Develop tools, guidance, documentation standards, and case management practices that support consistent and thoughtful decision-making.

• Partner Across the Business: Work closely with People Business Partners, Legal, and other People teams to navigate complex or high-risk employee matters.

Leaves & Accommodations

• Own the Programs: Lead Duolingo’s global leave of absence and workplace accommodations programs, including program strategy, employee experience, policies, processes, and continuous improvement.

• Lead Accommodations: Manage workplace accommodation requests from intake through implementation and follow-up, partnering with Duos and managers to identify effective, reasonable solutions.

• Navigate Complex Leaves: Serve as the internal expert and escalation point for complex leave matters, partnering with external administrators, Benefits, Legal, managers, and People Business Partners.

• Support Return to Work: Guide complex return-to-work situations and transitions between leave and workplace accommodations.

• Manage Vendor Performance: Establish clear expectations for external leave and accommodations partners and hold them accountable for service, accuracy, timeliness, and employee experience.

• Support Our Global Workforce: Partner with regional People Business Partners and Legal to navigate leave and accommodation matters across geographies and local requirements.

Insights & Program Improvement

• Surface Trends: Analyze employee relations, leave, and accommodation activity to identify recurring themes, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.

• Look Beyond the Case: Connect patterns across individual cases to broader questions about management practices, workload, role design, policies, benefits, accessibility, and the employee experience.

• Turn Insight Into Action: Partner with People leadership, PBPs, Benefits, and Legal to translate what we’re learning into practical improvements.

• Measure Effectiveness: Develop meaningful measures of program health, including timeliness, consistency, outcomes, employee experience, and vendor performance.

People Team Support

• Support PBP Priorities: Provide coordination and project support across select People Business Partner priorities, including documentation, reporting, research, and process work.

• Drive Follow-Through: Help keep defined PBP workstreams organized and moving, bringing strong attention to detail, judgment, and execution.

✅ You have...

• 5+ years of experience across employee relations, workplace accommodations, leave management, HR, or related areas, including experience independently managing complex employee matters.

• Experience conducting workplace investigations and navigating sensitive employee relations matters from intake through resolution.

• Strong working knowledge of workplace accommodations and leave practices, including the ADA, FMLA, and interactive process.

• Experience advising managers and People partners on complex employee situations and translating policies and legal requirements into practical guidance.

• Strong judgment and the ability to navigate sensitive or ambiguous situations with consistency and discretion.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including clear, objective case documentation.

• Strong case management and organizational skills, with careful attention to confidentiality and follow-through.

• Ability to identify patterns across individual cases and translate them into broader organizational insights.

• Comfort working across teams, functions, and geographies in a fast-moving environment.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Global Experience: Experience supporting employee relations, leaves, or accommodations across multiple countries or regions.

• Investigations Expertise: Significant experience independently conducting complex workplace investigations.

• Program Building: Experience building or scaling employee relations, leave, or accommodations practices.

• Vendor + System Management: Experience overseeing case management, external leave or accommodations administrators and using performance data to improve service.

• Systems & Insights: Experience using case management systems and employee data to identify trends and inform organizational decisions.

About the role...

The Duolingo English Test (DET) is a high-stakes assessment used by institutions around the world. Its integrity depends on proctors making accurate, consistent, and defensible decisions — even when sessions present ambiguous evidence or new forms of cheating. As the Proctor Quality and Learning Manager (L3) in Scaling Operations, you will own the end-to-end quality standard and learning system that keep our global proctor network aligned and effective as security threats, technology, and workflows evolve. You’ll define what “correct” looks like, run our calibration and adjudication program, and build ongoing training that measurably improves decision quality. You will partner with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering to ensure our human and AI-assisted workflows meet rigorous accuracy standards before and after deployment. This is an individual-contributor role within DET Proctoring Operations, with functional leadership over Training Specialists and adjudicators executing the program.

🧠 You will...

• Own the DET proctoring quality standard — maintain rubrics, decision rules, examples, and guidance that define accurate decisions across routine and difficult edge cases.

• Lead calibration and adjudication — operate recurring Proctor Certification Test cycles, resolve disputed decisions, identify patterns of disagreement, and ensure outcomes are consistent and auditable.

• Build and run an ongoing learning program — publish a forward-looking training calendar, deliver monthly interventions, and launch targeted training in response to quality signals, threats, or workflow changes.

• Measure effectiveness — use calibration results, audits, and performance trends to identify learning needs, evaluate training impact, and decide when to clarify standards, retrain, or update guidance.

• Guide specialist execution — set expectations for Training Specialists and adjudicators, assign deliverables, review outputs, and operate onboarding and certification that ramp new specialists quickly.

• Maintain durable sources of truth — keep calibration, adjudication, and training runbooks current so critical processes are documented and auditable.

• Evolve quality alongside proctoring — translate new threats and workflow changes into clear standards, training, and quality controls in partnership with Psychometrics, Security, Operations, Product, and Engineering.

• Represent the proctoring craft — bring frontline proctor evidence into product experiments and workflow decisions; assess whether launched changes preserve decision quality.

• Connect human and technology-assisted quality — establish benchmarks for AI-assisted workflows and validate automated capabilities against real sessions before deployment.

✅ You have...

• 5+ years in assessment development, scoring/rater quality, certification, quality assurance, or a field involving complex, consequential judgments; experience aligning reviewers to a shared standard through calibration programs.

• Adult-learning program experience spanning onboarding, certification, ongoing training, remediation, and effectiveness measurement (beyond one-off materials).

• Exceptional attention to detail and strong judgment in ambiguous cases; ability to produce clear, defensible decisions and guidance.

• Analytical fluency to interpret quality data, disagreement patterns, and performance trends and translate them into practical interventions.

• Clear written and verbal communication; ability to turn complex standards into precise, usable guidance and explain difficult calls.

• Cross-functional leadership without formal authority; experience directing contractors or partners toward clear accountability and outcomes.

• Demonstrated skill in quality standards and rubric design, building living systems with decision logs, change histories, and controls for auditability.

• Experience defining quality benchmarks and validation methods for human–technology workflows, including AI-assisted processes.

• Adaptability — comfort revising standards and programs as risks, products, and technology change.

⭐ Exceptional candidates will have...

• Experience in language assessment, test security, remote proctoring, trust and safety, or fraud prevention in high-integrity environments.

• Experience maintaining quality across large, distributed examiner/rater/reviewer/contractor populations.

• Familiarity with assessment concepts such as inter-rater agreement, reliability, standardization, and performance monitoring.

• Experience designing quality systems that span human judgment and technology-assisted workflows.

• Familiarity with learning-management systems, assessment platforms, quality-audit tools, or operational analytics.

About Watershed

Watershed is the enterprise sustainability platform. Companies like Airbnb, Carlyle Group, FedEx, Visa, and Dr. Martens use Watershed to manage climate and ESG data, produce audit-ready metrics for voluntary and regulatory reporting including CSRD, and drive real decarbonization. We are looking for team members who love product-building, want to work hard at a mission-oriented startup, and will collaborate with us in shaping the culture of a growing team.

We have offices in San Francisco, New York, Denver, London, Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Mexico City, and remote team members across the US and Europe. We hope that you'll be interested in joining us!

The role

Watershed is on a mission to help companies measure, reduce, remove, and report their emissions. We're looking for a strategic operator to join Customer Operations, which runs the programs that deliver on that mission for hundreds of enterprise customers.

You'll partner closely with Customer leadership to design and build the operational backbone for all three teams in our Customer organization: Customer Success, Sustainability Advisory and Services, and Support. That means the engagement models, scalable systems, forecasting infrastructure, and AI-driven workflows the team runs on, plus the reporting leadership uses to steer the business.

This is a role for a hands-on operator who builds what they design and has already rewired their work around AI. You'll operate as a trusted advisor and force multiplier for Customer leadership, owning initiatives end to end from framing the problem to standing up a working solution the team actually uses. You'll help guide the Ops roadmap rather than working a queue, with real scope to define what modern Customer operations looks like at Watershed.

Success means a Customer organization where structural calls like coverage and staffing are made with evidence rather than instinct, customer health scoring actually changes decisions, teams spend their time on customers instead of manual processes, and AI is embedded in how the team operates day to day.

You'll report to the Head of Customer Operations and join a small team of operators who each support a slice of the Customer organization.

This role is based in our New York or San Francisco office, with an expectation of 4 days per week in office.

You will:

• Design and implement the Customer operating model. Partner with Customer leadership across Customer Success, Advisory, and Support on:

• Organizational design, segmentation, and customer engagement models

• Capacity, staffing, and headcount planning

• Target setting and performance frameworks

• Own forecasting from the ground up. Retention, expansion, and services capacity - the methodology, models, and operating cadences that leadership actually trusts, and that surface risk and opportunity early enough to change the outcome

• Build AI-first operational workflows across the customer lifecycle, along with internal tooling that changes how the team operates day to day

• Lead strategic initiatives end to end. Drive complex, multi-workstream Customer org initiatives from conception through implementation. You'll frame problems alongside cross-functional partners, and co-build and co-own the result rather than handing over a recommendation

You might be a fit for this role if:

• You bring 5+ years experience in GTM Operations (CS Ops, RevOps, Strategy & Ops) at a high-growth B2B technology company, or a mix of top-tier strategy consulting and GTM Ops

• You've supported customer-facing teams directly, especially Customer Success. You know how CSMs actually spend their week, you've owned the reporting and operating cadence behind a retention number, and you can tell a real risk or expansion signal from noise

• You have demonstrated analytical excellence. You've built the forecasting models behind real leadership decisions, e.g., capacity, retention, expansion

• You turn ambiguous problems into working systems. You independently take a vague strategic objective through to a plan, a build, and adoption - often as the only person on the problem - and you hold strong opinions about what good looks like

• You're hands-on with GTM and BI tools like Salesforce, Gong, and Sigma. You build your own systems and partner with GTM Engineering on the bigger lifts. Bonus if you're adept with SQL and Salesforce administration, including automation and data model design

• AI is already embedded in how you work. You've shipped AI workflows that other teams actually use, and you have a point of view on how Customer teams should evolve because of it

• You're an exceptional communicator who influences without authority. You can drive alignment across Customer, Product, Data, Sales, and Finance when teams disagree

Must be willing to work from an office 4 days per week (except for remote roles)

Watershed has hub offices in San Francisco, New York, London, and Mexico City and satellite offices in Denver, Sydney, Paris, and Berlin. Where we have offices, employees are expected to be in office for 4 days per week. Certain jobs are open to being remote and will be specifically noted on the jobs page and in the job description if so.

What’s the interview process like?

It starts the same for every candidate: getting to know the team members through 1 to 2 conversations about Watershed, your experience, and your interests. Next steps can vary by role, but usual next steps are a skill or experience interview (e.g. a coding interview for an engineer, a portfolio review for a designer, deeper experience call for other roles) which leads to a virtual or in person interview panel. We prioritize transparency and lack of surprise throughout the process.

What if I need accommodations for my interview?

At Watershed, we are dedicated to ensuring an inclusive recruitment process. We provide reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities, long-term conditions, mental health needs, religious observances, neurodivergence, or pregnancy-related support requirements. If you need assistance during your process, please contact your recruiter.

Patreon’s security team works to protect Patreon creators and their fans. The team deals with all facets of Patreon’s security, including application security, infrastructure security, and internal/corporate security. We’re a small but effective team. We write code to solve security problems and work closely with our partners across the engineering organization. We also understand the importance of balancing security risks against business needs. We strive for honest and effective communication and focus on pragmatically reducing risk over checking boxes. The security team is part of Patreon’s Risk Engineering org, which also includes our Safety Engineering and Identity and Access teams. Collectively, the risk org tackles a range of problems including content moderation, internal tooling, identity verification, access control, and account security.

In this role, you’ll be a member of our Security team. You’ll split your time between contributing to security projects and responding to security investigations, vulnerabilities, or questions. The work spans application security, infrastructure security, and internal/corporate security. It includes both proactive and reactive security work. You’ll be part of an on-call rotation and help respond to security incidents and investigations. You’ll write code – both to support security work and to improve the security of the Patreon platform. You’ll work closely with other members of the security team, the wider Risk engineering org, and cross functional partners in engineering, legal, and IT. Your work will help reduce known risks and will protect the security, privacy, and trust of Patreon creators and their fans.

• You have two or more years of experience reducing security risks in the application, infrastructure, or corporate security spaces. You can create a threat model and to explain why a given risk matters and what we might do to reduce it.

• You have experience using AI tools (LLMs, ML models, etc) to identify and address security issues (software vulnerabilities, detection and response, etc.)

• You’re energized by fast iteration: shipping MVPs, testing hypotheses, and evolving products based on what creators and fans respond to.

• You take pride in creating elegant solutions to messy, real-world problems and balancing pragmatic trade-offs between security risks and business needs.

• You believe in Patreon’s mission: giving creators control over their work and building communities that feel good to be in.

• Edit episodes, with attention to pacing, framing, clarity, tone, structure and visual continuity and storytelling

• Give final sign-off on episodes and social clips

• Collaborate with the executive producer and hosts on setting editorial agenda and guest selection

• Work closely with producers to help them do their best work on deadline while they juggle their many responsibilities

• Anticipate challenges in episodes and proactively solve them

• Be a true partner for the executive producer

• May have input into staffing decisions and will be required to assess performance and provide feedback to staff

• Welcome feedback, incorporating editorial notes quickly, working cooperatively and coming up with creative solutions when disagreements arise

• Experience navigating a newsroom environment and solid news judgment

The Senior Engineer, Cybersecurity is a hands-on contributor who designs, builds, and operates security controls and services that protect The Times' systems, data, and users. As a member of the Security Architecture team, you will own complex initiatives end-to-end, drive measurable risk reduction, and collaborate across product engineering and enterprise technology with technical depth, operational rigor, and clear communication aligned with business outcomes.

Who are we?

Cybersecurity helps prevent The Times from becoming news. Our teams work to protect the news makers, their support staff, the platforms they rely on every day, as well as all of The Times' products and services, and our readers who consume them.

This role reports to the Director of Engineering, Cybersecurity.

Responsibilities:

• Create an environment that favors context, not control. Empower product engineers and ensure they have the relevant information and tools to deliver secure products and services.

• Design, implement, and operate security controls and services (e.g., identity and access management, secrets management, endpoint/agent hardening, network segmentation, detection, and response automation) that meet reliability, security, scalability, and observability standards.

• Partner with product and platform teams to integrate security into architecture and developer workflows while articulating business impact and tradeoffs.

• Perform security reviews, threat modeling, and risk assessments (code, design, 3rd-party apps).

• Investigate and resolve urgent and/or complex security issues, triaging effectively and driving architectural changes that prevent recurrence.

• Participate via RFCs, community of practices, and other internal knowledge sharing channels to share learnings, align on standards, and influence secure patterns across areas; model The Times' core values in cross-functional collaboration.

• Support team growth through peer design/code review, pairing, and clear feedback; on security engineering practices across the department.

• Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

• 5+ years of experience in software engineering and security engineering space.

• Understanding of security controls across a variety of security domains, including access management, encryption, vulnerability management, AI security, network security, authentication/authorization.

• Knowledge of one or more Cloud platforms (AWS, GCP) and best practices for architecting and securing.

• Experience with software engineering practices (CI/CD, GitOps, IaC, etc.) and related security practices (SAST, SCA, secure by design, shift left, etc.).

• Programming skills in at least one language (Go, Python).

• Experience with containerization and orchestration platforms.

• A bias towards helping people. Many teams will rely on you to help build their systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Security/Compliance or DevOps certifications

• Experience with Kubernetes

• Experience with Terraform and Packer

• Experience with HashCorp Vault

This role may require limited on-call hours. An on-call schedule will be determined when you join, based on team size and other factors.

This is a hybrid remote/in-office role.

• Maintain supporting schedules and documentation for payables, prepaid expenses, and other assigned accounting activities.

• Identify unpaid invoices and gather information to support the accounting team’s preparation of month-end accruals.

• Verify account coding and transaction dates against established guidelines, escalating unusual or unclear items.

• Research reconciling differences and help resolve missing, incomplete, or inaccurate transaction records.

• Keep invoices, approvals, payment records, reconciliations, and other supporting documents complete and accessible.

• Review transaction reports for missing information, duplicate entries, and other potential errors.

• Retrieve records and prepare supporting documentation for audit, tax, and other accounting requests under the accounting team’s direction.

• Follow established approval procedures and financial controls, promptly flagging exceptions or discrepancies.

• Handle confidential vendor, payment, and business information with discretion.

Improve how the work gets done

• Identify practical ways to improve data accuracy, simplify routine reconciliations, and reduce manual work.

• Assist with testing accounting system updates and changes to established workflows.

• Support responsible use of approved automation and AI tools, verifying outputs before use.

• Maintain clear process documentation and provide backup support for related accounting tasks as needed.

Overview:



ZRG Aspen Leadership Group is proud to partner with the Amargosa Conservancy in the search for an Executive Director.


Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will lead the organization through an important leadership transition while building upon more than two decades of conservation impact across the Amargosa Basin. The ED will provide strategic, operational, and financial leadership while serving as the organization’s primary ambassador, relationship builder, and champion for its mission. The Executive Director will lead a talented staff team, cultivate strong partnerships, strengthen organizational sustainability, and represent the Conservancy with a wide range of constituents, including community members, Tribal Nations, government agencies, elected officials, conservation partners, funders, and supporters.


Working closely with an actively engaged Board of Directors and a highly capable staff, the Executive Director will oversee fundraising and revenue diversification, strategic planning, organizational development, communications, financial stewardship, and external relations. The role requires a collaborative leader who can navigate complexity, bring together diverse perspectives, and identify common ground among communities, conservation interests, Tribal Nations, resource management agencies, elected officials, and other stakeholders.


The Executive Director will play a central role in strengthening the Conservancy’s long-term sustainability by deepening relationships with funders and supporters, broadening the organization’s funding base, supporting a culture of staff development and collaboration, and helping guide strategic priorities for the future.


The Amargosa River is often described as a miracle of the desert. Flowing through one of the driest landscapes in North America, the river and its springs sustain an extraordinary network of wetlands, wildlife, cultures, and communities found nowhere else on Earth. From the headwaters near Beatty, Nevada, to the wetlands of Ash Meadows and the vast landscapes of Death Valley, the Amargosa Basin is a place where water gives life to people, culture, and biodiversity in remarkable and unexpected ways.


For more than 22 years, the Amargosa Conservancy has worked to protect the wilds, waters, and communities of the Amargosa Basin through science, stewardship, advocacy, and community engagement. Today, the Conservancy serves as a trusted voice for conservation and a respected partner to local communities, Tribal Nations, scientists, land managers, policymakers, and fellow conservation organizations working to safeguard the future of this remarkable place.


Today, the Amargosa Conservancy stands at an exciting moment in its history. With a dedicated staff, engaged board leadership, strong community partnerships, and growing regional influence, the organization is poised for its next chapter. The Conservancy is financially strong, with significant reserves and approximately two years of organizational runway, providing stability and flexibility as it looks to the future. The next Executive Director will have the opportunity not only to protect an extraordinary landscape, but also to build upon a foundation of conservation success, organizational strength, and community trust while helping shape the future of a region, its communities, and the life that depends upon it.


Qualifications:


A bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience and at least five years of progressive leadership experience is required. While experience in conservation, public lands, environmental advocacy, natural resources, Tribal engagement, rural communities, government relations, or related fields is beneficial, the Amargosa Conservancy places greater value on leadership, relationship-building, sound judgment, emotional intelligence, and a demonstrated commitment to the mission. Candidates who bring curiosity, adaptability, and a genuine appreciation for the people, culture, and landscapes of the American Southwest are encouraged to apply.


The Amargosa Conservancy will consider candidates with a broad range of backgrounds. If you are excited about this role and feel that you can contribute to the AC, but your experience does not exactly align with every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply. All applications must be accompanied by a cover letter and résumé. Cover letters should be responsive to the mission of the Amargosa Conservancy and the responsibilities and qualifications specified in the position prospectus.

The salary range for this position is $115,000 to $125,000 annually. The Amargosa Conservancy offers a stipend for health insurance and generous paid time off.

BACKGROUND ON THE ENVIRONMENTAL INTEGRITY PROJECT


The Environmental Integrity Project (EIP) is America’s environmental watchdog. We are a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting public health and our natural resources by holding polluters and government agencies accountable under the law. We advocate for tough but fair environmental standards and empower communities fighting for clean air and water.


Our team of lawyers, analysts, engineers, and communications professionals provide support to communities fighting David vs. Goliath battles against some of the biggest polluters in the U.S. We sue not only corporations that don’t follow the law, but also federal and state agencies when they fail to do their jobs to protect public health and the environment.


POSITION OVERVIEW


EIP is accepting applications for an Environmental Engineer to join our team working to hold industrial polluters and federal and state agencies accountable for compliance with the Clean Air Act and other environmental laws. Working with EIP’s team of lawyers and analysts, the Engineer will work to reduce pollution from industrial sources through regulatory, permitting, and enforcement strategies. EIP takes legal action to clean up pollution; we publish data-driven reports that push federal and state regulators to better protect public health; and we work with frontline communities to provide the resources they need to obtain the protection of our environmental laws.


EIP is a national organization with strong partnerships with frontline communities and organizations in the Gulf States, Ohio River Valley, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic regions. We are dedicated to reducing the enormous amount of climate, air, and water pollution generated by the fossil fuel power sector and industries that extract, store, or process oil or natural gas to make fuel, chemicals and plastics, fertilizers, and other petrochemical products. EIP work also targets pollution from other sectors, including steel manufacturing, landfills and trash incinerators, and aluminum production. EIP’s Center for Applied Environmental Science (CAES) ensures that local communities and environmental advocates have access to high-quality science and engineering expertise.


The Engineer position will support these programs and can be based in Washington, DC or remote. The position may require occasional travel throughout the U.S.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




• Work with EIP’s legal team, analysts, and external experts to develop factual, technical, and scientific support for citizen suit enforcement and other advocacy efforts. 

• Research and draft technical memos, comments, and reports related to Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act violations at industrial facilities. 

• Provide technical support for communities impacted by air pollution from industrial operations. 

• Manage client and community relationships and work effectively within coalitions. 

• Work with EIP’s communications and research teams to develop and execute communications strategies and investigative reports. 


QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS




• Must hold a degree from an ABET-accredited engineering program. 

• 10+ years of environmental engineering experience or experience in related fields, including but not limited to civil engineering, chemical engineering, and/or petroleum engineering. 

• Strong preference for engineers with experience developing and supporting enforcement actions to address violations of the Clean Air Act and other environmental laws. 

• Excellent analytical, research, writing, organizational, oral communication, and interpersonal skills. 

• Demonstrated commitment to protecting public health and the environment. 

• Ability to work collaboratively with colleagues and external partners. 

• Strong work ethic, robust problem-solving skills, and sound judgment. 


COMPENSATION


EIP offers competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and a supportive working environment. Salary is based on a nonprofit scale and is commensurate with skills and experience. For this position, the salary range is $105,000 – $132,000.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY


EIP is an equal opportunity employer. As an equal opportunity employer, EIP is committed to employment practices that ensure that employees and applicants for employment are provided with equal opportunities without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, age, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other factor that is not related to the position.


APPLICATION PROCESS


Qualified candidates should submit their application materials here: Engineer Application . Applications should include:




• A current resume; 

• Cover letter explaining your interest in this position; and 

• A writing sample. 


EIP will accept applications on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is a pioneer in its approach to mental health treatment. In addition to providing superior Clinical care from the nation’s most talented and passionate clinicians, Charlie Health offers unparallelled and effective holistic treatment via our groundbreaking Integrative care including Contemplative, Creative Arts, and Experiential Programming. We firmly believe that thriving, sustainable health is the result of treating the whole person - mind, body, and spirit - and our vIOP deeply embodies this philosophy. As such, we advocate for and provide inclusive, accessible, diverse, cosmopolitan healing approaches that transcend the conventional Western psychological model. Charlie Health’s synergistic Clinical + Integrative treatment model affords cutting edge mental health care that proudly serves our amazing clients.

Charlie Health is excited to expand its Contemplative Programming Department. Aligned with the growing bodies of research that evidence positive psychological transformation as a result of contemplative interventions and practices rooted in wisdom traditions, our Contemplative Practitioners support our clients in developing mindful awareness, cultivating wisdom, discovering purpose, living compassionately, and practicing self-inquiry. Some of our current therapeutic modalities include Yoga Therapy, Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction, Mindful Self Compassion, Breathwork, Philosophical Consultation, Transpersonal Psychology, Spiritual Coaching, Meditation, and Chaplaincy. Some of the modalities we are eager to include are Contemplative Psychotherapy, Contemplative Arts, Dreamwork, Depth Psychology and many more.

Charlie Health is hiring a few exceptional Contemplative Practitioners to provide remote, telehealth services to our clients. We’re eager to work with forward-thinking mental health and substance use professionals to enhance our programming and provide the best possible care to our clients.

This is a contract / 1099 position that allows you the flexibility to schedule sessions and work wherever you are most comfortable. We request that our facilitators are able to dedicate at minimum 9 permanent group hours per week to facilitate group sessions and build valuable connections with our clients.

People know Charlie Health for our warm and empathetic team. While each individual facilitator has their own interests, expertise, and style, we require all team members to be well versed in a variety of therapeutic modalities. Our clients are struggling to cope with underlying mental health issues and benefit from facilitators that are sophisticated and relational. Successful candidates are committed to bettering the mental health of their clients, and are adept at self-care, ensuring they are prepared to give their best every day to address the rural mental health crisis.

About You

• Able to demonstrate expertise in your contemplative practices (e.g. Yoga Therapists (C-IAYT), Yoga Teachers (RYT), Mindfulness (MBSR), Mindful Self-Compassion (MSC), etc.) and feel confident integrating them into your treatment approach

• Confident and experienced in working with a wide range of ages, including children, teens, young adults, and adults

• Passionate about the benefits of group practices and skilled in conducting group sessions

• Ability to work effectively in a team

• Creative and engaging, especially over video!

Qualifications

• Clinical experience and/or experience in mental health or behavioral health is required for this role. Please do not apply if you do not meet this qualification.

• Must be available during late afternoons and evenings on weekdays (3-8pm MT on Monday to Thursday) and on Saturdays to meet the schedules of our clients

• Experience with a wide range of ages, including children, teens, young adults, and adults is required

• Experience with high acuity populations is required

• Must be certified in your contemplative practice (all disciplines are welcome to apply), and/or hold a Clinical license

• Minimum 3 years of teaching/facilitating experience in your contemplative field

• Master’s degree in Mental Health

• Availability between 9 and 40 hours per week

• The technical ability to run effective Telehealth sessions

• Reliable WIFI connection when meeting with clients

• 1099 Position, part time with opportunity to grow into full time position

• Familiarity with and willingness to use cloud-based communication software—Gmail, Slack, Zoom, Dropbox–in addition to EMR and survey software on a daily basis

• Work authorized in the United States and native or bilingual English proficiency

• Partner with Revenue Systems to build policy into system rules, validations, and alerts, reducing manual reviews and after-the-fact corrections.

• Improve forecast methodology by tracking actual results against the forecast, explaining variances, and changing processes that aren't working. Partner with Finance and Revenue Analytics to reconcile the field forecast with the finance outlook.

• Own the weekly forecast readout for the CRO and sales leadership, keeping it short and focused on decisions. Bring the forecasting and policy perspective into annual planning.

• Coordinate the CRO organization's weekly, monthly, and quarterly reviews, metrics, and follow-ups. Measure their impact on pipeline hygiene, data quality, forecast accuracy, and bookings, and change the cadence where it isn't working.

• Work with other Revenue Strategy & Operations teams, Finance, Product, Data, and Enablement to deliver changes from the first draft through field adoption. Keep cadence documentation current so the organization knows what happens when, who owns it, and what's expected.

• Mentor others on the team and improve how we document and run our processes.

What you’ll bring

• Experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, management consulting, or a similar role, including running a forecast process day to day in a business-to-business (B2B) subscription business.

• A practical understanding of how a sales organization runs, including pipeline stages, deal bookings and crediting, bookings and annual recurring revenue (ARR) definitions, and how compensation influences sales representative behavior.

• Strong data and analysis skills. You're highly proficient in Excel or Google Sheets, can build a model from scratch, and check your own numbers before sharing them.

• The ability to work independently, identify what needs to be done, and work with stakeholders to get it done. You involve your manager when you need a decision or hit a blocker.

• Clear, concise writing. You can turn a complex issue into a short document or Slack message that a senior leader will read and act on.

• Comfort working with senior leaders, including taking feedback from a CRO and turning it into a better process or a more useful readout.

• Systems thinking and the ability to learn new tools and domains quickly. How you think matters more to us than which forecasting tool you've used.

An overview of this role

As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.

What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.

What you do

• Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team

• Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review

• Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.

• Own the architecture of the program model (parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis) and of the pipeline that turns source code into findings, and define how both extend to new languages and frameworks

• Solve technical problems of the highest scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, UX, and partner teams such as Code Security and Composition Analysis

• Mentor all engineers on the team through code review and pairing, remove blockers to their autonomy, and shepherd the definition and improvement of our internal standards through review

• Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues

• Define the overarching architecture and specification documents for the engine, delegate component specifications within them, and drive their implementation by AI agents and engineers working independently through phased plans, small reviewable units of change, and specifications kept in lockstep with the code

• Build and maintain the harness, agent instructions, and agentic skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy, including separate coding and reviewing agents, rules and tests the coding agents cannot change, independent review panels of agents from different model providers, and performance, API, and dependency gates, with risky changes escalated to human review

• Stay current with research in program analysis and security, run AI-assisted research and spikes, and turn the findings into prototypes, proposals, and upstream contributions, including responsible disclosure of findings in open source projects

What you bring

• Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't

• Extensive professional experience writing, testing, and reviewing production code in Rust, Go, or a comparable systems language, with depth in at least one. The engine is Rust, the analyzer wrapper is Go, and the monolith integration is Ruby, and we value willingness to work across them.

• Experience with performance optimization and with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)

• A deep program analysis and static analysis background, such as parsing and ASTs, intermediate representations (SSA, control-flow and call graphs), taint and data-flow analysis, type inference, incremental and fixpoint computation, or writing detection rules, with the ability to read, evaluate, and apply the research literature

• Deep application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE)

• Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems, and to write architecture and design specifications that bring a team to a decision

• A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous, team-wide problems and shipping them from concept to production with minimal guidance, with specific, regular async updates on progress, blockers, risks, and next steps

• Experience defining a system's overarching architecture, delegating component specifications to engineers and AI agents, and getting them implemented reliably

• A track record of mentoring engineers, raising a team's technical bar, and influencing technical direction by achieving consensus with peers and leadership

Helpful experience

• Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration

• Experience designing guardrails for agent-written code, such as mutation testing, fuzzing, and CI gates the coding agent cannot modify

• A record of engaging with the research community, such as publications, tool papers, or upstream open source contributions in program analysis or security

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories.

About the role

Join us to build the decision engine for better mental health outcomes.

As a Senior Data Scientist, you will sit in the heart of a cross-functional product team and help turn messy, real-world signals into clear decisions. You will make sure we are capturing the right data, designing experiments that tell us what is actually driving outcomes, and translating findings into recommendations that teams can act on quickly. When the insight is stable and valuable, you will help operationalize it through predictive models that improve provider and patient experiences.

We’re looking for people who like ambiguity, enjoy hard problems, and want their work to matter in the world.

What you will do

• Be the analytics partner inside the pod. Work closely with Product, Engineering, Design, Ops, and Clinical stakeholders to define the questions, the metrics, the guardrails, and the decision rules.

• Design and analyze A/B tests and quasi-experiments with clear hypotheses, power considerations, and pre-defined success criteria.

• Connect behavior to strategy. Use funnel, cohort, segmentation, and lifecycle analysis to understand how people and providers experience Headway, and where product changes will have the biggest impact.

• Use causal inference when experiments are not possible. Apply approaches like diff-in-diff, matching, and regression-based designs with principled uncertainty quantification.

• Develop predictive models that operationalize vetted insights (feature development, validation, backtesting, calibration), with clear launch criteria and monitoring plans.

• Produce analysis and narratives that are crisp, honest about uncertainty, and drive action.

• Help raise the bar by contributing to shared standards for metrics, experimentation, and analytical quality, so teams can move faster with confidence.

What will make you successful

• 6+ years using data to drive product or business decisions in product, growth, health, engineering, or operations environments.

• Strong SQL and strong proficiency in Python or R for analysis and modeling.

• Depth in experimentation and causal inference under real-world constraints.

• Fluency with AI tools as part of your workflow: using LLMs and coding assistants to accelerate analysis, prototyping, and documentation, while still owning the judgment and rigor behind the output.

• Practical modeling skill: feature engineering, model comparison, cross-validation or backtesting, calibration, and post-launch monitoring.

• Strong product sense and opinions, including a track record of connecting analytics recommendations to measurable outcomes.

• Clear communication: you can explain complex work to non-technical audiences without losing the truth.

• A self-starter mindset: you prioritize well, follow through, and do not need heavy oversight.

• Motivation for our mission: improving access and affordability in mental healthcare.

Where you could land

Data Science at Headway is structured around three core pillars, each focused on a distinct area of the business. Within each pillar, smaller pods own specific problem spaces, and several of those pods are actively hiring. We keep our interview process consistent across teams, and ahead of your preliminary call we’ll share a pre-read with details on the specific pods that are hiring so we can talk through where you might fit best.

• Patient: The Patient group owns how someone finds mental health care on Headway and gets to a provider who fits them: the first visit or phone call, search and matching, booking, and then attending a first appointment and staying in care. Data Science here means consumer funnel analytics, experimentation, and marketing science. That includes defining the metrics the group steers by, designing and reading experiments, and building causal and attribution methods for channels where you can't cleanly randomize. The modeling work spans ranking, matching, propensity, and the lifetime value and attribution models behind how we spend to acquire patients.

• Payer & Outcomes: The Payer & Outcomes group is responsible for driving best-in-class patient outcomes, building a trustworthy and safe provider network, and delivering value-based care with responsible costs relative to outcomes, both through product work across the company and by working directly with payers. On the Data Science side, there's room to go deep on product data science, commercial data science, or a mix of both: experimentation, causal modeling, forecasting, and sizing work. People are often drawn to this team by its rapid growth and by how directly the day-to-day work ties back to Headway's mission.

• Provider: Providers have real choices about where they build their practice. A provider might join Headway for credentialing, stay for reliable payments and tools that make the day easier, find new clients or bring over existing ones, or grow into a group practice. The Provider group owns that relationship and the trust it depends on, because we believe a clinician who feels supported can better help their patients. Data Science here is about understanding those choices: what draws a provider in, what keeps them, and what helps them grow with us. Experiments usually run at the provider level and often pair a product change with a conversation. Causal inference fills the gaps where randomization isn't possible. The models cover lifetime value, attribution, churn, and how providers respond to rates and incentives, along with work on how our tools support providers and their patients. Because the work spans product and go-to-market, Data Scientists here see the full provider relationship.

About the Web Platform team at Headway

Web Platform owns how Headway builds our frontend applications, including the UX. Web Platform sits in our Engineering Foundations organization, alongside our infrastructure and reliability team and our agentic engineering team. Every engineer who builds for the web at Headway builds on top of our work. When the platform is strong, product teams move faster and ship with higher quality. As the platform evolves to incorporate agentic engineering workflows, the team is positioned to become an even greater multiplier: using agents to build front-end code directly in line with Headway's standards, reducing the time and cognitive load product teams spend on front-end concerns so they can focus on business logic and product outcomes.

The team works across three areas:

• Design system: Helix is the shared language between Design and Engineering. Its components, tokens, and patterns keep what we design and what we ship the same across every Headway web app.

• Web architecture: We give engineers one clear way to build a Headway web app. This covers frameworks, build tooling, data loading, testing, performance, and accessibility across our patient, provider, internal, and marketing apps.

• Agentic UI: Headway engineers build with AI agents every day. We want those agents to build UI to Headway's standards by default. That takes a design system, patterns, and docs that agents can read, plus automated checks (visual regression, accessibility, and design system conformance) so that agent-written UI ships with confidence.

Principles that guide us:

• Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing.

• Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration.

• Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.

• Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

Tools we use:

• Languages: TypeScript

• Libraries & Frameworks: React, React Router 7, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Helix (our design system)

• Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry

• Version Control: GitHub

• AI Tools: Cursor, Claude, Gemini, Eddy (our in-house cloud agent harness)

Who you are

Architect and own the cloud platform that every engineer at Headway deploys on. Make deploys boring, scaling automatic, infrastructure self-serve, and cost attributable.

About Infrastructure Engineering at Headway

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. Infrastructure Engineering is one of three teams in Engineering Foundations, alongside Agentic Engineering and Eddy, Headway's internal AI platform. We own the infrastructure Headway runs on, as well as the performance and scalability of Headway's FastAPI/Python monolith, and the AWS infrastructure it runs on. We are the paved road the rest of engineering builds on: databases, deploys, asynchronous platform, observability, autoscaling, and self-serve compute infrastructure.

As AI dramatically increases code velocity across the org, our mandate is to make every change safe from the start and build systems that get safer as they get faster.

About This Role

You will be on the Infrastructure team, which owns the cloud platform Headway runs on. You will be the senior engineer driving work to isolate blast radius, make autoscaling trustworthy, and build a self-serve infrastructure platform so that the Infrastructure Engineering team focuses on the strategic and unusual, not the routine.

What You'll Own

• Deployment architecture and blast-radius containment. Redesign deployment so that a mistake in one part of our service cannot block or take down others. Continue to drive our shift toward per-service deploy isolation and functional-area slices that contain failures rather than propagating them across the platform.

• Container footprint and networking. Own the ECS and EKS footprint, evaluate broader EKS adoption for AI workloads, and design the next iteration of inter-service network connectivity.

• Capacity and scaling. Own capacity for a spiky workload: floors computed ahead of demand rather than chased by reactive scaling, self-deriving from data, with drift caught early.

• Self-serve infrastructure platform. Build the Terraform self-serve platform with guardrails so engineering teams own their standard infrastructure changes and Reliability Engineering reviews only the non-standard ones.

• Cloud cost attribution and controls. Stand up per-team cost attribution across AWS, Datadog, and LLM spend. Make infrastructure costs visible and attributable so teams can make informed tradeoffs.

• Python runtime and dependency health . Own how the monolith behaves under load: garbage collection, event loop contention, and the runtime limits that bite first. Lead the framework and package upgrades most teams defer.

Who You Are

A senior engineer who combines deep cloud and infrastructure expertise with the instincts to drive alignment across teams. You thrive in ambiguity, operate with a high degree of ownership, and are as comfortable setting technical direction as you are building. You make other engineers better through architecture reviews, runbooks, and paved-road tooling that raises the baseline for everyone who ships on the platform.

Experience we're seeking:

• 5 or more years in platform, infrastructure, or SRE roles at companies running significant production traffic

• Deep AWS expertise and production ownership of compute and networking at scale (ECS, EKS, RDS, networking, IAM)

• Strong infrastructure-as-code experience, particularly Terraform, including designing self-serve platforms for other engineering teams

• Hands-on autoscaling and capacity engineering, and container orchestration with ECS and/or EKS

• Track record making deploys safe and self-serve for other teams, not just your own

Nice to have:

• FinOps and cloud cost optimization experience

• Kubernetes and EKS depth

• Observability tooling at scale (Datadog)

• Experience in healthcare or other regulated environments

Partner with Security and product teams on anomaly detection and response, weighing engineering cost and user impact alongside the benefit of any control.

• 5+ years as a Software, SRE, Platform, or Infrastructure Engineer, with a track record of owning reliability outcomes for production systems that customers depend on.

• Hands-on depth in observability and SLO engineering: golden signals, burn-rate alerting, journey-level monitors, and turning noisy alert streams into actionable pages (Datadog preferred; Prometheus/Grafana and OpenTelemetry welcome).

About the Role:

The best SDETs in the industry are no longer measured by how many tests they write. They're measured by the systems they build that decide whether software is safe to ship — and, increasingly, by how well they wield AI to do it.

That's the role we're hiring for. We're looking for a Senior Staff SDET to own quality architecture and engineering strategy for our most critical systems, and to lead how we apply AI across our entire testing and release pipeline. You'll build the frameworks, platforms, and agent-driven workflows that the rest of engineering depends on, define what "safe to ship" means here, and stay deep in the code while doing it.

This is a genuinely hands-on senior technical leadership role with impact that spans many teams. If you want to build AI-native quality systems rather than bolt AI tools onto a legacy suite, this is that job.

Why This Role Is Different

• AI is the core of the work. You'll own how we use LLMs and agents for test generation, failure triage, self-healing, and release decisioning — and you'll set the guardrails that keep it trustworthy.

• You'll test AI, not just test with it. We ship AI-powered product features, which means building evaluation harnesses, golden datasets, and probabilistic assertions for systems that don't return the same answer twice. This is frontier work with very little established playbook.

• Real autonomy and real scope. You'll set the technical direction for quality engineering, not inherit someone else's strategy.

You Will:

Own quality architecture and strategy

• Own quality architecture for our most critical systems and initiatives, defining long-term quality strategy aligned with business and product goals.

• Design shared quality platforms, automation frameworks, and test infrastructure that are adopted across multiple teams.

• Establish quality patterns and guardrails that scale across teams, eliminating duplicated, brittle, or low-signal testing approaches through platform-level solutions.

• Anticipate systemic quality and reliability risks and drive preventative architectural solutions before they impact customers.

• Set the standard for what "great" looks like in quality engineering at scale.

Lead our AI-driven testing strategy

• Define and drive our strategy for AI-assisted testing — autonomous test generation, intelligent test selection, agent-based failure triage, and self-healing automation — with a clear-eyed view of where each genuinely pays off and where it adds noise.

• Build the guardrails that make AI-driven testing trustworthy: knowing when a self-healing agent is masking a real regression versus absorbing harmless implementation drift is the difference between leverage and liability.

• Orchestrate AI agents as part of the CI/CD decision pipeline, turning raw test signal into release confidence rather than more dashboards.

• Own quality for our AI-powered product features — designing eval suites, golden datasets, LLM-as-judge scorers, and statistical approaches for non-deterministic behavior, plus testing for hallucination, safety, and response stability.

• Establish how we test AI-generated application code, validating behavioral correctness and not just syntactic plausibility.

• Evaluate emerging AI testing tooling with real rigor, and be honest about what doesn't work.

Raise the bar operationally and across the team

• Lead the operational maturity of our quality systems and signals — defining quality metrics, dashboards, and release confidence indicators, and leading post-incident analysis that informs architectural and process improvements.

• Produce exemplary technical artifacts — quality architecture documents, automation frameworks, test platforms — that set the bar for the rest of the team, while staying hands-on in critical quality systems and automation code paths.

• Serve as the accountable technical leader for strategic initiatives, proactively managing reliability, scalability, and technical debt across teams.

About the Role:

We are seeking a highly motivated, detail-oriented Manager, Production Planning to lead the planning team responsible for our non-sterile compounded production. This position manages and develops the site's production planners and owns the forward-looking production plan. The plan converts demand forecasts and inventory policy into a rolling view of the next several weeks through the next year or more, tests that plan against labor, equipment, and material capacity, and identifies where the business cannot meet it. The Manager then drives the response to each gap, whether through training, labor, or capital investment, and hands the plan to Production Scheduling for on-site execution. The ideal candidate is a proactive people leader with a strong understanding of integrated planning systems, supply chain dynamics, and cross-functional collaboration across the operations planning team.

You Will:

• Lead, manage, and develop the team of production planners, setting priorities, coaching, reviewing output, and ensuring consistent planning practices and coverage.

• Own the development and maintenance of mid- and long-term production plans for non-sterile compounded products in alignment with demand forecasts and inventory policies.

• Define the planning horizons, plan-of-record cadence, and frozen window, and publish the plan to Production Scheduling on a fixed schedule.

• Manage finished goods inventory for compounded products within company guidance while maintaining click-to-deliver metrics for customers.

• Develop what-if scenarios that identify where and when the plan exceeds available capacity, and which constraints are most sensitive to demand, product mix, batch size, and shift patterns.

• Articulate and document all risks resulting from production capacity constraints, including volume at risk, timing, and effect on delivery and inventory. If the plan cannot be met, make or recommend revisions when plans cannot be met, and document the reason for each revision.

• Recommend and size actions to close each gap, including training and cross-training for skill coverage, hiring and labor planning, overtime and shift design, equipment and facility investment, and outsourcing. Partner with Compounding Operations, HR, and Quality to carry out approved actions and track whether each one delivers the capacity it was sized to deliver.

• Monitor plan attainment, forecast accuracy, and capacity utilization at the weekly and monthly level, analyze variances, and implement corrective actions.

• Use actual cycle times, yields, and throughput reported by Production Scheduling to update planning standards and capacity model assumptions.

• Collaborate cross-functionally across the operations planning team, partnering with demand planning to communicate forecast discrepancies and agree on the plan of record, with production scheduling to confirm the plan can be executed and take in the constraints it escalates, and with procurement and raw materials planning to confirm material availability.

• Develop and maintain tools, dashboards, and KPIs that communicate plan status, constraints, risks, and performance to plan to leadership.

You Have:

• 8+ years experience in at least 1 of the following: Production planning, capacity planning, or resource planning, with demonstrated experience leading or developing others.

• Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Industrial Engineering, or related field required; APICS/CPIM certification a plus.

• Experience building capacity models and presenting investment, staffing, or outsourcing recommendations to senior leaders.

• Proficient in inventory management concepts with an understanding of the financial and operational implications of planning decisions.

• Experience in pharmaceutical or pharmacy production/manufacturing environments is a plus.

• Excel proficiency including experience with data manipulations – Lookups, PivotTables, External Data Connections.

• Basic SQL and/or Python experience is a plus.

• Deep knowledge of supply chain and manufacturing planning processes.

• Strong analytical skills and comfort with data-driven decision making.

• Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities and lead a team in a fast-paced environment.

Computer and live video tools literacy (e.g., Zoom, Google Meets, DoxyMe, Skype, etc.)

About the Role:
Lyra developed an innovative video therapy program called Lyra Care Therapy: Blending live video sessions with between-session digital psychoeducation and customizable skill building tools. The Lyra Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) program capitalizes on Lyra Care Therapy to supplement standard individual DBT and DBT skills groups with novel between-session DBT-relevant digital activities—activities that help promote skill generalization and integration into your clients’ daily lives. Lyra DBT clients also have 24/7 access to a team of licensed clinicians who have been trained in DBT skills coaching for around the clock support.
As a Lyra DBT Therapist, you’ll provide individual DBT and DBT skills groups via live video to adolescent clients. You’ll also assign DBT-relevant digital lessons, videos, and assessments to your clients to enhance learnings and monitor outcomes between sessions. Lyra's clients come from a multitude of backgrounds and experiences, and have varying needs and abilities. We strive to continue to meet their unique needs by delivering culturally responsive care—an approach that accounts for the impact of cultural backgrounds on each person’s care experience.
Our therapists enjoy connecting with their colleagues who share a passion for providing evidence-based care. You’ll attend weekly consultation team meetings as well as one-on-one consultation meetings with an expert DBT team lead, co-lead DBT skills groups with other DBT providers, and attend robust trainings to enhance your clinical skills. You always have a team behind you if a crisis comes up. You’re never alone, even while working remotely in the US.
This role is a great fit if you’re a MA licensed DBT clinician who enjoys working with complex clients in a supportive, collaborative, and feedback rich environment. You may also find this role rewarding if:
- You are passionate about helping others improve their lives through skills-based interventions and work to understand your clients through a lens of compassion and curiosity.
- You enjoy evidence-based practice, continual learning, and professional improvement.
- You prefer to work within a collaborative team environment.
- You are accountable for your own outcomes and performance, and are willing to embrace challenges that others may shy away from.

•
Unrestricted, active Massachusetts license (able to work independently without supervision from a licensed supervisor) without current or pending disciplinary action

•
Formal didactic training in DBT required (e.g., in-house training with consultation team, tape review, 1:1 supervision; Behavioral Tech; DBT Foundational Training; DBT Intensive Training)

•
One year minimum experience providing comprehensive DBT to adolescents which includes: individual DBT therapy with clients through Stage 1 of treatment, facilitating skills groups utilizing Linehan materials, participation on a consultation team, skills coaching

•
DBT-LBC certification preferred but not required

•
Experience, comfort, and passion working with clients who present with high risk behaviors, including suicidal ideation and/or self-injury

•
Willingness to obtain cross-licensing in additional states as needed to support program growth

•
Experience providing telehealth therapy services in a virtual environment (video and teletherapy) preferred but not required

•
Computer and live video tools literacy (e.g., Zoom, Google Meets, DoxyMe, Skype, etc.)

Provide clear, evidence-based diagnostic impressions and actionable recommendations tailored to the individual’s needs

•
Deliver compassionate feedback through feedback videos and live sessions to communicate findings and recommendations

•
Maintain a detail-oriented, process-focused approach to ensure the accuracy of testing data and comprehensive reporting

Utilize telehealth platforms effectively for remote assessments, including adapting testing strategies for virtual delivery

•
Conduct intake interviews, testing sessions, and live feedback sessions, delivered virtually or in person, as indicated

Doctorate degree in Psychology (PhD or PsyD) from an American Psychological Association or Canadian Psychological Association accredited program

•
Licensed Clinical Psychologist in at least one state

•

•
3+ years of experience in psychological assessments with children, adolescents, or adults

•
Familiarity with evaluating complex behavioral health needs (e.g., ASD, ADHD, mood disorders, anxiety, trauma)

Expertise in psychological and psychoeducational assessment tools (e.g., BASC, Conners, WAIS, WISC)

Effective therapeutic communication skills

•
Experience conducting testing virtually

Ability to deliver care virtually or in person and within your own office space

You'll develop and execute bold, insight-driven 360° marketing campaigns that bring our brand to life across every channel—from NYFW to wedding season to summer travel and beyond. You'll design and produce our tentpole events and community programming that deepen customer connection and spark cultural conversation.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is part strategist, part operator, part community builder—who thrives in the details, loves turning strategy into action, and moves seamlessly between big-picture thinking and execution. You'll play a key role in how women discover and experience Rent the Runway, translating business priorities, consumer insights, and product stories into impactful campaigns, events, and brand moments that drive brand relevance and business growth.
